question: An organization is undergoing an audit against ISA/IEC 62443-4-1 for their secure product development lifecycle. The auditors find that the development team lacks a formal process for handling third-party software components. Which of the following actions should the organization take to align with the standard? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Ignore third-party software security, as the primary vendor is responsible for all code.
Establish a process for monitoring vulnerabilities in the integrated third-party libraries.
Create a Bill of Materials (BOM) for all third-party software used in the components.
Implement a systematic approach for updating or replacing vulnerable third-party components.

source_explanation: The 62443-4-1 standard requires visibility and control over third-party software. Creating a BOM allows for tracking components, monitoring ensures vulnerabilities are identified, and a replacement process ensures that identified risks are mitigated. Ignoring third-party security is a major failure in a modern development lifecycle, as supply chain vulnerabilities are a high-risk vector. • A. Create a Bill of Materials (BOM) for all third-party software used in the components. • D. Implement a systematic approach for updating or replacing vulnerable third-party components.
